svg.title: Trust boundaries
svg.desc: Agents connect with their own scoped credential and you with Touch ID, your password or a passkey. Both reach your providers only through hoistd, which checks access, asks you before anything that can't be undone and journals every change. On your computer, provider tokens sit in the OS credential store; on a remote, a separate credential keeper holds them in a sealed file. hoistd itself is trusted.
svg.text: · hoistd is trusted. If it's compromised, its own checks can be skipped.
· The keeper guards where tokens are kept, not which actions run.
· Connecting or importing an account passes its token through hoistd once.
· Revoking an agent doesn’t revoke your provider tokens.
· Your computer's admin, or the server's, can read what hoistd can.
· Stopping Hoista doesn’t undo changes a provider already made.
